title: CPM Analyst Chat: Ten Minutes On, MP 214.3

fields.topic: Prairie Bend segment MP 196–231 · CPM-PB alarm follow-up

messages.text: Got the RATE-OF-CHANGE on PT-2143 and the CPM-PB imbalance. Pulling trends now. Confirmed: no pump trip on PL-MAINLINE-PUMPS, no movement on BV-2131 or BV-2156, no WO-PB work order open on the segment.

The Wabash hi-level is the LT-WJT-N01 gauge problem on ticket WJT-27-04418. It isn't connected to this. The imbalance is FT-196 in vs FT-231 out on the Prairie Bend segment, not the Wabash receipt. PT-2143 is at 821 psi, and imbalance is 2.2 % and climbing.
PT-2143 is at 814 psi. PT-2131S and PT-2156 are both still trending down. No packing or rebound like you'd see after a transient.

06:02. Ten minutes on. Pressure at 214.3 hasn't recovered (now 812 psi). Imbalance is now 2.6 % and rising. I can't rule out a leak, and I can't locate it either. The model's location estimate runs from MP 209 to MP 219, so it covers both sides of the river. Nobody in the field has eyes on anything. No confirmed loss, no cause. Your call.
Page sent and delivered to on-call Qualified Individual Teresa Holloway: "PRAIRIE LINE MP 214.3 POSSIBLE LEAK — CCSS DECIDING SHUTDOWN." Acknowledgment: pending.

instructorNote: This is the decision point. The 10-minute window has run out and a leak can't be ruled out. Watch for the CCSS to shut down the line by 06:04 and close Mill Ridge and Sandhill by 06:09 without waiting to find the cause (Response Plan section 4, step 2). Then the CCSS, as person in charge, should call the NRC by 06:17, log the call time and report number, and only after that call the QI. The QI should not hold up the NRC call and should start the Level 2 IMT call-out.
